Analysis description: data: Every 5 minutes the server records the BTC price. For each 5-minute interval the page takes how much BTC moved (in %) and how many longs and shorts the trader account opened in that interval.
Analysis description: shift: For every shift from −120 to +120 minutes it computes the Pearson correlation r between these two series. A positive shift means BTC moved first and the trades were opened that many minutes later; a negative shift means the trades came first and BTC moved after them.
Analysis description: sign: r > 0: more trades are opened when BTC rises; r < 0: when BTC falls. Even a real link is usually small: r = 0.1 means BTC moves explain only about 1% of how the number of opened trades varies.
Analysis description: noise: The dashed lines are the noise band: two unrelated series stay inside it 95% of the time. Because the best of 49 shifts is picked, its p-value is multiplied by 49 (Bonferroni correction), and only a result with adjusted p < 0.05 is reported as a link.
Analysis description: limits: Only the trader (master) account is counted. A short period such as one day gives a wide noise band, so pick a week or more for a firm answer. A link is not profit: the page shows whether the trader reacts to BTC, not whether that earns money.
Analysis description: levels: Why not the BTC price against the number of open positions: two trending series correlate by accident, with any sign, so such a chart changes its answer from period to period. Changes and newly opened trades do not have that problem.
Closed trades describe: Trades CLOSED on the selected day (your time zone): realized PnL, mean ROE per trade, number of trades and the share of profitable ones. The public main page counts the same way, by UTC days.
